reference: Bash type/help and the published killall interface define metadata expectations. All selection/delivery operations remain deferred to a disposable VM or reviewed non-forwarding proc/signal adapter; no psmisc GNU parity result is claimed.
coverage: Bash recognizes killall as a builtin when PATH is empty.
Bash help metadata advertises exact comm matching, supported selectors, and the default TERM signal.
Deferred operation requirements cover exact matching, full command lines, real UID filtering, option and signal parsing, errors and proc races, and controlled delivery.
exclusions: No parity case invokes GNU psmisc killall or the candidate because either may signal a process.
No operation is claimed to pass; all process selection and delivery behavior is deferred pending a disposable VM or non-forwarding syscall/proc mock.
killall5, pkill, and other loadables are outside this suite.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify the injected killall command as a builtin; the harness runs with an empty candidate PATH.
Bash help metadata must describe the documented exact-name behavior, command-line and UID modes, and default signal without invoking killall.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help killall)
[[ $help_text == *"Signal every process with comm exactly equal to any NAME."* ]] || exit 21
[[ $help_text == *"-e, --exact"* ]] || exit 22
[[ $help_text == *"-f         match against /proc/PID/cmdline"* ]] || exit 23
[[ $help_text == *"-u USER    only signal processes whose real uid is USER"* ]] || exit 24
[[ $help_text == *"Default: TERM"* ]] || exit 25
printf 'exact-comm\nfull-command-line\nreal-uid\nterm-default\n'

cases.purpose: Check the core matching contract, including exact comm equality, similar-name exclusion, multiple names, duplicate names, the 15-byte comm boundary, self-exclusion, and default SIGTERM.
cases.reason: No killall run exists. Legacy runner inside the VM: bwrap private PID namespace means only fixture processes are visible, so killall NAME cannot reach anything outside the case. psmisc killall 23.7 is installed in the image as the oracle.

cases.purpose: Exercise -f exact joined-command-line selection, including NUL-separated arguments, empty arguments, long records, and substring nonmatches.
cases.reason: -f is a candidate extension (psmisc 23.7 killall has no -f option), so there is no GNU oracle; it needs a contract case with owned children.

cases.purpose: Check -u numeric and account-name filters against real UID records, including a nonmatching UID and filter interaction with name selection.
cases.reason: Numeric and name filters with matching/nonmatching UIDs are implementable for uid 2000; real-vs-effective distinction requires root-prepared credentials.

cases.purpose: Check default TERM, signal names with optional SIG prefix and case variation, numeric signals, -e/--exact compatibility, and usage errors such as zero or unknown signals/options.
cases.reason: No parsing case runs. Parser errors can be compared without any target; valid signals need trap-logging children.

cases.purpose: Check no-match, usage, and fatal-proc status classes along with malformed or missing proc records, bounded PID parsing, delivery ESRCH/EPERM, and partial success.
cases.reason: No killall status path executed. EPERM and no-match are reproducible in the VM; malformed records and ESRCH require a fixture proc adapter with a non-forwarding kill recorder.

cases.purpose: Qualify real signal delivery and cleanup only against a uniquely named direct child whose PID, parent, UID, and comm are independently verified immediately before delivery.
cases.reason: The disposable VM plus bwrap private PID namespace satisfies the isolation the original reason required; no executed fixture exists.
